key_insight: OmniStream introduces a unified streaming visual backbone that uses causal spatiotemporal attention to simultaneously perceive semantics, reconstruct 3D structure, and drive action in real-time continuous streams.
problem_solved: Addresses the fragmentation of vision foundation models (separate image perception, offline temporal models, and geometric pipelines) by providing a single causal, physically structured representation for live, multi-task visual agents.
method: Causal spatiotemporal attention backbone that processes continuous visual streams with temporal causality and memory for online inference.
Shared representation that branches into integrated modules for semantic perception, geometric reconstruction (spatial/3D reasoning), and action/control.
Multi-task/self-supervised pretraining on diverse streaming data and lightweight online state updates to enable low-latency, generalizable behavior.
impact: Makes it practical to build single models that handle perception, mapping, and action in real time—reducing system complexity, improving latency and sample efficiency for robotics, AR, and autonomous systems.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: streaming inputs → causal spatiotemporal attention backbone → three heads (perception, reconstruction, action).
Timeline visualization showing causal attention and memory propagation across frames for online inference.
Before/after qualitative panels: raw frames → reconstructed 3D geometry over time → action outputs (e.g., navigation or manipulation).
Comparative bar chart: unified OmniStream vs. specialized baselines on latency, accuracy, and multi-task efficiency.
paper_title: OmniStream: Mastering Perception, Reconstruction and Action in Continuous Streams
paper_authors: Yibin Yan, Jilan Xu, Shangzhe Di, Haoning Wu, Weidi Xie
